title: Synchronize Portal UI and current documentation with permanent Qwen3 model contract
audit_findings: At base HEAD the Portal backend MODEL_CATALOG is already correct and exposes exactly qwen3-32b and qwen3.8-27b with model:qwen3:chat.
Portal chat model selector, chat default/model hints, API-key model choices, helper text and examples remain hardcoded to qwen-14b and qwen-32b-base in active/current frontend artifacts.
Dashboard/agent surfaces call /api/v1/models, but the chat selector is not using that authoritative catalog.

No evidence was found that browser localStorage, service worker, cached static JSON or build-time model environment variables are the primary catalog source; stale source content itself is sufficient to reproduce the drift.
Current documentation contains stale Qwen2.5/qwen-14b/qwen-32b-base/model:32b:chat claims and examples.

docs/operations/DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md points to a Stage-15 frontend manifest while deploy/portal-frontend-combined.html represents a later frontend generation; production/canonical frontend source must be established from runtime facts and documented consistently.

runner-live/runner-status.json is absent from GitHub at the base HEAD. Do not fabricate this file in this corrective task; its absence is a separate Source-of-Truth observability gap, not proof that the runner is down.
objective: Make every active Portal user-facing model surface and every current-facing project document consistent with the accepted permanent model set qwen3-32b + qwen3.8-27b, with scope model:qwen3:chat and exact model routing, while preserving historically correct evidence, dated snapshots, acceptance reports and rollback assets.
forbidden_paths: docs/evidence/** except the two exact R1 evidence paths listed in allowed_paths

historical_preservation_rule.rule: Old model names may remain only where they are explicitly historical, superseded, migration-related or rollback-only. Current architecture, current operations, user guides, examples and active UI must not present them as available models.

implementation_requirements: First prove from live runtime and repository which frontend artifact/deployment is actually serving the Portal. Record deployment/workload, mounted source/config and content fingerprint without printing secrets.
Do not change the already accepted Portal backend model catalog or routing unless a concrete regression is proven. Backend verification is read-only for this task.
Make /api/v1/models the authoritative source for the chat model selector. Do not maintain a second hardcoded active model list for chat.
The rendered chat selector must contain exactly qwen3-32b and qwen3.8-27b after authenticated catalog load.
Use user-facing labels Qwen3-32B and Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 while preserving exact API IDs qwen3-32b and qwen3.8-27b.
Use model:qwen3:chat for API-key scope UI and examples. Remove active/current model:32b:chat, model:14b:chat, model:32b:chat-adapter and model:32b:completion choices.
Remove qwen-14b/qwen-32b-base/Qwen2.5 from active selector options, defaults, welcome text, hints, diagnostics, API-key model choices and current examples.
If /api/v1/models cannot be loaded, fail closed: do not silently fall back to old or invented models; disable model-dependent send/create actions and show a controlled catalog-load error.
A deterministic default may be qwen3-32b when present; otherwise select the first model returned by the accepted catalog. Never use an unknown fallback model.
Do not use substring routing or infer an upstream from model text.

Reconcile the declared canonical frontend deployment source. If the Stage-15 manifest is no longer canonical, current deployment documentation must say so unambiguously; if it is canonical, update it so applying the documented deployment cannot restore stale UI.

Update current-facing documentation and examples only. For WUI_DUAL_MODEL_AND_AGENT_FLOW.md, preserve historical facts if it is an historical design record; mark it superseded and point to the permanent model contract rather than rewriting history if appropriate.
Do not regenerate or rewrite historical evidence/PDFs/screenshots merely because they contain old model names.
Do not create runner-live/runner-status.json in this task.
runtime_rules: No secrets in logs, commits, screenshots or evidence.
Do not read or print Kubernetes Secret values unless strictly necessary; it is not necessary for this task.
Do not use direct database access for authentication or API-key workflows.
Use normal Identity/API workflows for temporary credentials if runtime validation requires them and revoke/delete all temporary credentials afterwards.
Do not modify /root/.hermes, create another Telegram Gateway, grant generic sudo, set safe.directory=*, or change repository ownership to root.
Runtime claims require captured commands/results or equivalent machine-verifiable evidence.
Hermes must not self-commit or self-push; host runner performs finalization.
test_matrix: T01 repository/static scan: classify old identifiers as current vs historical; no current-facing stale model claim remains in allowed current docs/UI.
T02 backend read-only contract: authenticated /api/v1/models returns HTTP 200 and exactly qwen3-32b + qwen3.8-27b; Qwen2.5/qwen-14b/qwen-32b-base absent.
T03 UI catalog source: prove the chat selector is populated from /api/v1/models rather than a hardcoded second catalog.
T04 rendered UI/DOM: authenticated fresh session shows exactly Qwen3-32B and Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 and exact IDs qwen3-32b/qwen3.8-27b.
T05 fresh-browser/cache independence: new/private session or cache-bypassed fetch shows the corrected selector; record whether any cache invalidation was required.
T06 negative catalog load: failed /api/v1/models load does not fall back to old/unknown model; model-dependent action fails closed with controlled message.
T07 API-key UI: model authorization is represented by model:qwen3:chat; no obsolete model-specific scopes are offered as active choices.
T08 authenticated non-streaming chat qwen3-32b -> success.
T09 authenticated non-streaming chat qwen3.8-27b -> success.
T10 streaming chat for both active models -> success, if Portal UI exposes streaming in this deployed generation.
T11 invalid model -> HTTP 404 with model_not_found; no fallback route.
T12 deployment reproducibility: applying/following the current documented frontend deployment source cannot reintroduce the stale Stage-15/14B/old-32B UI.
T13 documentation: README, model catalog, API reference, deployment guide, current user guides and user package agree on two active models and model:qwen3:chat.
T14 historical preservation: sampled accepted historical evidence remains byte-identical/unmodified and old names there are retained as historical facts.
T15 cleanup: temporary API key/session/secret used for validation is revoked/logged out/deleted and reuse fails where applicable.

must_include: base HEAD and final worktree HEAD prepared for runner finalization
proof of live frontend deployment/source identity
static scan results with current-vs-historical classification
rendered selector/DOM evidence from a fresh session or equivalent served-page verification

acceptance_criteria: Backend/API contract still exactly qwen3-32b + qwen3.8-27b and exact unknown-model rejection.
Portal chat selector in the actually deployed UI obtains its active list from /api/v1/models and shows exactly the two accepted models.
No old model is user-selectable or presented as currently available anywhere in the active Portal UI.
Current API-key UI and current docs use model:qwen3:chat and do not direct users to obsolete model scopes.
Current README/architecture/operations/API/user documentation no longer describe Qwen2.5, qwen-14b or qwen-32b-base as active models.
Historical evidence and rollback facts remain preserved and clearly distinguishable from current state.
Canonical frontend deployment source is unambiguous and reproducible without restoring stale UI.
Required runtime/static evidence is complete, internally consistent and contains no secrets.
Only ChatGPT may issue PASSED / CONNECTOR VERIFIED / RUNTIME ACCEPTED / ACCEPTED after independent GitHub audit.
hard_prohibitions: No direct edits to accepted historical evidence or acceptance reports.
No substring routing or unknown-model fallback.
No modification of CURRENT_TASK files by Hermes.
No unrelated refactoring or roadmap work beyond this UI/docs synchronization.
